title: Functorial adjoint character-weight vectors over an arbitrary field
statement:
Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field] and $T,G$ be $k$-group schemes with a homomorphism $i:T\to G$ [def-sc-group-scheme]. Characters $\chi:T\to\mathbf G_m$ use [def-sc-gm-ga]. Write $\mathfrak g=\operatorname{Lie}(G)$ and $v_\epsilon\in G(k[\epsilon])$ for the actual tangent point of $v\in\mathfrak g$ [sk-d-tangent, def-wf-lie-algebra-derivation], using the dual numbers [def-sc-dual-numbers]. For every commutative $k$-algebra $A$ and $c\in A$, define $v_{A,c}\in G(A[\epsilon])$ by pushing $v_\epsilon$ along the $k$-algebra map $k[\epsilon]\to A[\epsilon]$ that sends $\epsilon$ to $c\epsilon$. For $s\in T(A)$, let $s_\epsilon$ be its constant extension to $A[\epsilon]$ and evaluate $\chi(s)\in A$ by the Laurent coordinate as in [def-sfb-rho-section-module-data]. Define the functorial adjoint character-weight vector set
$$W_i(\chi)=\{v\in\mathfrak g:\ i(s_\epsilon)v_{A,1}i(s_\epsilon)^{-1}=v_{A,\chi(s)}\text{ for every commutative }k\text{-algebra }A\text{ and every }s\in T(A)\}.$$
For a split torus this is the usual character-weight space, expressed as its set of vectors. This definition uses all test algebras, rather than just rational points, and imposes no restriction on the characteristic or cardinality of $k$.

source.place: Theorem 12.12 and Remark 12.13, pp.234--235, character weight spaces; Definition 21.26, p.433, adjoint roots and regular cocharacters. The dual-number formulation uses the actual tangent-point construction of sk-d-tangent.
